extracted.intended_audience: general readers, fans, and researchers of television and British comedy
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia article overviewing the British sitcom The IT Crowd, its genre labels, characters, production choices, reception, adaptations, and controversies — useful for analyzing the show's comedic strategies and production factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre (Sitcom / Black comedy / Surreal humour / Slapstick)
rubrics_metrics.description: The IT Crowd — Genre: Sitcom, Black comedy, Surreal humour, Slapstick
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explicitly classifies the show under multiple comedic modes; these labels indicate expected tone, pacing, and acceptable comedic devices (e.g., surreal non-sequiturs, dark/black humour, physical slapstick). Use these genre labels to judge whether individual episodes or scenes conform to the show's declared modes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Running gag / obscurity of company's business
rubrics_metrics.description: The obscurity surrounding the company's business is a running gag; it is stated that the company has bought and sold ITV, has a chemicals laboratory, and makes an unnamed product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recurring comedic device for the series is intentionally vague or inconsistent world-building about Reynholm Industries' business; evaluate humour that arises from this persistent ambiguity. Running gags should be recognizable, repeated, and used to generate escalating jokes or callbacks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of the IT staff ('standard nerds')
rubrics_metrics.description: Roy and Moss, the two technicians, are socially inept geeks or, in Denholm Reynholm's words, 'standard nerds'. Roy's support techniques include ignoring the phone and using reel-to-reel tape recordings of stock IT suggestions; Moss offers overly detailed technical suggestions and is shy with poor social skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedic effectiveness depends on consistent, distinctive character traits (Roy: slacker/irreverent; Moss: technical pedant/shy). Evaluate whether jokes arise organically from these traits and whether characters remain recognisable and true to their established quirks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jen's role as non-technical 'Relationship Manager' (comic role inversion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Jen Barber, the department head/relationship manager who knows nothing about IT, claims on her CV that she has 'a lot of experience with computers', often pronouncing the word as 'comp-you-ters'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The humour relies on role inversion and imposture: a manager who must bluff technical competence. Assess how well scenes exploit Jen's non-technical status for comic situations without undermining character credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of live studio audience / multi-camera production
rubrics_metrics.description: The show was video-recorded with a live studio audience. Camera setup: Multi-camera.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production format affects comedic timing, laugh-track dynamics, and staging. When evaluating or reproducing similar comedy, consider how multi-camera staging and audience reactions shape pauses, punchlines, and physical blocking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catchphrases and stock IT suggestions as comedic hooks
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of stock IT suggestions used for laughs include 'Have you tried turning it off and on again?' and 'Is it definitely plugged in?'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated catchphrases and recognisable stock lines function as comedic hooks and audience touchstones. Judge their effectiveness by recognizability, timing, and whether they are varied or subverted rather than overused to the point of stagnation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptation success criteria: translation, direction, timing, performance
rubrics_metrics.description: The German version was criticised for the poor translation of the original stories and jokes, poor direction, poor timing, and the poor performance of the actors, mainly Stefan Puntigam as Gabriel (the German version of Moss).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adaptations should preserve joke intent and timing; key measurable dimensions are translation quality (faithful transfer of humour), directorial choices (pace and visual framing), comedic timing, and actor performance. Failures in any of these areas are cited as causes of poor reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content sensitivity / modern appropriateness (controversy over transphobic themes)
rubrics_metrics.description: All episodes of the programme are available to stream in the United Kingdom and the Republic of Ireland on All 4, except the fourth episode of series three, 'The Speech', which was removed from Channels 4's streaming service on 4 October 2020 for perceived transphobic themes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate humour against contemporary standards of sensitivity; episodes or jokes that provoke perceptions of bigotry may be removed or criticized. This is a criterion when judging lasting acceptability and distribution viability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards and nominations as measures of critical success
rubrics_metrics.description: The IT Crowd has won awards from the British Academy of Film and Television Arts (BAFTAs), the International Academy of Television Arts and Sciences (the International Emmys), the Rose d'Or television entertainment awards, and fan-voted Comedy.co.uk Awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognition via industry awards and nominations is an external metric of a show's quality and reception. Use awards and critical scores (e.g., Metacritic) as one axis among others (audience response, longevity) when evaluating the series' success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extended world-building and transmedia humour (DVD menus, Easter eggs, extras)
rubrics_metrics.description: DVD start-up sequence and menus are designed to resemble a ZX Spectrum; menus parodied 8-bit and 16-bit games and included hidden extras encoded into subtitles, JPG images, and a text adventure game file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedic identity can be reinforced through creative extras and transmedia elements. Evaluate these for coherence with the show's humour, inventiveness, and ability to reward engaged fans (e.g., Easter eggs, parody menus).

rubrics_metrics.name: Casting and actor performance impact on comedic reception
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism of the German version singled out 'the poor performance of the actors' as a reason for negative reception; similarly, cast chemistry and performances are highlighted throughout the article (main cast: Chris O'Dowd, Richard Ayoade, Katherine Parkinson, Matt Berry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actor casting, delivery, and chemistry are core criteria for comedy's effectiveness. When evaluating episodes or adaptations, assess whether performances support timing, character humour, and the intended tone.
